result.summary: The image shows a wide, four-lane residential street with sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and street lighting exists, the environment is dominated by vehicle travel lanes with no visible marked crossings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a refuge island or marked crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: High Speed Environment
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway with multiple lanes and minimal friction encourages higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings with high-visibility paint and signage to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features an exceptionally wide concrete walkway that is in a state of significant disrepair, with deep cracks and encroaching vegetation. It is situated between a residential brick building and an expansive parking lot, separated only by a low curb and lacking any shade, seating, or high-quality pedestrian infrastructure.

hazards.name: Surface Degradation
hazards.description: Extensive cracking and uneven pavement with grass growing through the joints create significant tripping hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire foreground and middle ground walkway.

hazards.name: Lack of Vertical Separation
hazards.description: The absence of bollards or substantial barriers between the wide walkway and the adjacent parking lot may allow vehicles to encroach on the pedestrian space.
hazards.location_in_image: Left edge of the walkway along the curb line.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and resurface the concrete walkway to provide a smooth, accessible, and hazard-free path for all users.

interventions.title: Green Infrastructure Buffer
interventions.description: Introduce a bioswale or a row of street trees between the walkway and the parking lot to improve aesthetics, provide shade, and create a physical buffer.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install shorter, more frequent light poles to ensure the wide walkway is well-lit at night, improving safety and security.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, with a grass buffer on the left, but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. The wide roadway and lack of intersection controls suggest a car-oriented environment where vehicle speeds may be high.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated crossing points for pedestrians along this stretch of road.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The generous width of the roadway likely encourages higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street may obscure pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections or appropriate mid-block locations to provide designated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees in the buffer zone to provide shade, improve aesthetics, and create a psychological narrowing effect to slow traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of basic infrastructure on the near side of the roadway, with no visible sidewalk or marked crossings. The wide travel lanes and absence of traffic calming measures create a hostile environment for people walking, particularly at the uncontrolled alleyway entrance.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway on the near side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and left side of the image along the road edge

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The entrance to the residential alleyway lacks any pedestrian crossing markings or signage, creating conflict points with turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image where the alley meets the main road

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the near side of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks across the main road and the alleyway entrance to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at the alleyway entrance to shorten crossing distances and slow turning vehicle speeds.
